name: Paris
summary: Paris grew from Lutetia, a Roman town on an island in the Seine, into the capital of the Frankish kings and then of France itself. It gave the world Notre-Dame and the Sorbonne, the storming of the Bastille and the Terror, Haussmann's boulevards and the Eiffel Tower. Occupied and liberated within living memory, it remains a world capital of art, ideas and style on the river that has always defined it.

figures.label: Population
figures.note: City of Paris; ≈11 million in the Île-de-France metropolitan region.

figures.label: Founded
figures.note: As Roman Lutetia; renamed Paris, after the Parisii, in the 4th century.

figures.label: Setting
figures.note: Île-de-France, in the north of France.

figures.label: World Heritage
figures.note: The riverfront from the Louvre to the Eiffel Tower.

figures.label: Known for
figures.note: A world capital of culture for centuries.

events.title: Roman Lutetia
events.body: Rome conquers the Gaulish Parisii and builds the town of Lutetia on the Seine’s island and left bank.

events.title: Julian and the name “Paris”
events.body: Roman troops here proclaim Julian emperor; over the 4th century the town takes the name of its people, the Parisii.

events.title: Sainte Geneviève
events.body: By tradition Geneviève rallies the townsfolk, and their prayers turn Attila’s Huns away from Paris.

events.title: Clovis makes it his capital
events.body: The Frankish king Clovis settles Paris as the capital of his new kingdom.

events.title: The Vikings sack Paris
events.body: Norse raiders sail up the Seine and pillage the city; more sieges follow.

events.title: Notre-Dame begun
events.body: Construction starts on the great cathedral of Notre-Dame de Paris.

events.title: The Sorbonne
events.body: Robert de Sorbon founds the college that anchors the famed University of Paris.

events.title: The Black Death
events.body: Plague devastates Paris, killing tens of thousands.

events.title: An English coronation
events.body: During the Hundred Years’ War the boy-king Henry VI of England is crowned king of France in Paris.

events.title: St Bartholomew's Day Massacre
events.body: Thousands of Protestants are slaughtered in Paris during the Wars of Religion.

events.title: “Paris is worth a Mass”
events.body: Henri IV converts to Catholicism and enters Paris, ending the religious wars.

events.title: The court leaves for Versailles
events.body: Louis XIV moves the royal court out of Paris to his new palace at Versailles.

events.title: The Bastille falls
events.body: A Paris crowd storms the Bastille on 14 July, igniting the French Revolution.

events.title: The king guillotined
events.body: Louis XVI is executed on today’s Place de la Concorde; the Terror follows.

events.title: Napoleon crowned
events.body: Napoleon crowns himself Emperor of the French at Notre-Dame.

events.title: The Arc de Triomphe
events.body: Napoleon’s great triumphal arch is finally completed.

events.title: Haussmann remakes Paris
events.body: Baron Haussmann drives broad boulevards and sewers through the medieval city.

events.title: The Paris Commune
events.body: A radical commune governs Paris for two months before being crushed in a bloody week.

events.title: The Eiffel Tower
events.body: Built for the World’s Fair, the tower becomes the enduring symbol of Paris.

events.title: The Métro and the Belle Époque
events.body: The Paris Métro opens as the city dazzles the world at another World’s Fair.

events.title: The Treaty of Versailles
events.body: The peace ending the First World War is signed just outside Paris.

events.title: The Nazi occupation
events.body: German troops march into Paris; the occupation lasts four years.

events.title: The Liberation
events.body: Allied and Free French forces liberate Paris in August 1944.

events.title: May 1968
events.body: A student revolt and general strike shake the French state to its foundations.

events.title: The Pompidou Centre
events.body: A radical modern-art museum opens, part of a wave of grand cultural projects.

events.title: The Louvre Pyramid
events.body: I. M. Pei’s glass pyramid opens for the bicentenary of the Revolution.

events.title: The November attacks
events.body: Coordinated terrorist attacks across the city kill 130 people.

events.title: Notre-Dame burns
events.body: Fire ravages Notre-Dame; a global effort begins to restore it.

events.title: The Paris Olympics
events.body: Paris hosts the Summer Games a century after it last did, in 1924.

places.name: Île de la Cité
places.note: The island in the Seine where Roman and medieval Paris began.

places.name: The Louvre
places.note: Royal palace turned the world’s most-visited museum.

places.name: The Bastille
places.note: The fortress-prison whose fall in 1789 began the Revolution.

places.name: The Eiffel Tower
places.note: Built for the 1889 World’s Fair; the symbol of Paris.

caveats: This timeline is compiled from general reference works — listed under Sources — rather than an event-by-event archive of primary documents, as the Mumbai timeline is. Treat it as a reliable outline, not a citation of record.
Dates for the earliest, legendary events are traditional rather than documented.

dynasties.note: Dynasties and houses that shaped Paris.

list.name: The Capetians
list.legacy: Paris as the fixed capital of France
list.summary: The line that made Paris the permanent capital of France and raised its first great monuments.

list.name: House of Bourbon
list.legacy: Royal Paris — before the court left for Versailles
list.summary: Henri IV and Louis XIV shaped Paris before moving the court to Versailles; the Revolution ended their reign.

list.name: House of Bonaparte
list.legacy: The Arc de Triomphe and Haussmann’s boulevards
list.summary: Napoleon I and III crowned themselves in Paris and reshaped it, from triumphal arch to grand boulevards.
